★★★★★★ **TWO OF MY OWN §UI-4 CLAIMS WERE WRONG, AND THE SECOND ONE MATTERED MORE THAN THE DEFECT I WAS FIXING.**

**① `dst == 0` IS NOT A CHANNEL DISCRIMINATOR — A CONVERSE ERROR.** I verified that *every channel producer passes `dst = 0`* and concluded *`dst = 0` ⇒ channel*. That is the converse and it is false: **six unrelated operations emit exactly `{dst = 0, ctr = 0}`** — `send_layer`'s `unsealable` arms at `node_mac.cpp:220/452/473/561/579` plus `node_mac.cpp:59/111`. A matcher built on it attributes a colliding `send_layer` refusal to the alarm and lands it in TERMINAL `Emergency::failed` — **the same false negative I was closing, reached by a different route.** ⇒ ★ **THE REUSABLE RULE: a gate check must enumerate everything that EMITS the value, not everything the feature touches.** Owner ruling: **`match_channel_failed` is DELETED and must not be reintroduced** — a ctr-less async `send_failed` is not attributable, and the core says so outright ("the reason arrives asynchronously and correlates with nothing", `node_channel.cpp:~723-744`).

**② "IT FAILS SAFE TO NOT HEARD" WAS FALSE — IT WAS AN INFINITE RETRY LOOP (register B84).** Arithmetic, not opinion: `UiModel::_tries` increments **only** in `on_send_accepted` ("ACCEPTED transmissions, never requests"), and a `ctr == 0` send never reaches it. So my `tick()` produced `seal failure → awaiting → 8 s → channel_remote_mint → re-queue → awaiting → 8 s → …` **for ever with `attempts() == 0`**, because `_tries >= kEmgMaxTries` can never become true. **Unbounded airtime on the distress path — in that one dimension worse than the permanent `SENDING...` it replaced.** ⓘ And the preflight half of my story was right: those refusals *are* synchronous (`exec_command` → `refuse_reason_of` → `on_send_refused` → `Emergency::failed`, reason intact). Only the **post-mint** seal failure is async, and it has already burned a counter the caller never sees.

⇒ ★★★ **THE RULE IMPLEMENTED: an expired unattributable EMERGENCY consumes ONE bounded attempt BEFORE its `channel_remote_mint` is processed.** Three expiries spend the three-alarm budget and terminate in sticky `NOT HEARD` with no fourth request queued. It matches the approved *"accepted by the transmitter is what we can establish"* policy and fails safely — if the missing push really was a failure, an attempt has been honestly spent. ⓘ **Owner accepted the cost: this rare path loses its precise terminal reason**, so `SendOutcome::channel_failed()` now has **no producer** (it survives in the model for UI-3's synchronous shape; recorded, not removed — that file is Task 3's).

★★★★★ **THE RULE LIVES IN THE CALLER'S ORDER, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDED FOUR INTEGRATION CASES AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL.** `_tries` is the model's and the ordering is UI-6's, so no unit test of either alone can reach it. The suite now carries: **(1)** a colliding `send_layer {dst = 0, unsealable}` cannot make the emergency `failed` — every remaining matcher is offered the push and refuses it, so the guarantee is **structural** (no entry point exists) rather than a comparison; **(2)** each `ctr == 0` expiry consumes exactly one attempt (`attempts()` 1, 2, 3 — not 0); **(3)** three expiries terminate in sticky `NOT HEARD`; **(4)** no fourth request is queued. ★ Plus a deliberate **NEGATIVE CONTROL** that asserts the *defect* shape (`attempts() == 0`, still `firing`, a fourth request queued) — so "the suite is green" and "the retry path is bounded" can never again be mistaken for one fact, and any future change that moves `_tries` elsewhere turns it red.

★★★★★★ **THE HEADLINE IS A DISAGREEMENT WITH BOTH THE PLAN AND THE BRIEF, AND IT CHANGED THE WORK: `SendOutcome::channel_remote_mint()` — §B68's whole point, added by UI-3 — HAD NO PRODUCER, AND THE PLAN'S TRACKER COULD NOT GIVE IT ONE.** The brief's first "thing that will bite" says *"`SendOutcome::channel_remote_mint` is the kind for it — render as SENT, never PICKED UP"*. Measured: the plan's tracker emits **eight of the nine kinds and never that one**, and a tree-wide grep found **zero** callers of the factory. Worse, the state it belongs to is the one the plan never closes. Verified in the source, not inferred — `node.cpp:1631-1634` on producer (3): a registered mobile's delegated GLOBAL post *"emits no CHANNEL-level push at all, only the wrapper DM's own send_acked/send_failed, under a ctr this caller never saw"*. ⇒ **an `awaiting` slot on that path can never be closed by any push, so the alarm sits on `SENDING...` FOR EVER — §B72's defect one level up, on the same safety path, and reached by a success rather than a failure.** ⓘ `kOutcomeWindowMs`'s own comment promised *"how long an accepted send may still claim a ctr-less outcome"*; nothing in the plan ever consumed the expiry. **Fixed by `bool tick(now_ms, SendOutcome&)`** — the window's expiry, and the ONLY producer of the eighth kind. It reports a **SUCCESS shape** deliberately (§B68: *"a tracker that maps `ctr == 0` to failure calls a delivered message failed"*), and it is safe on the alarm path as a **property of UI-3 rather than an assumption**: `on_outcome` routes `channel_remote_mint` through the `channel_no_relay` branch ⇒ bounded retry, then `NOT HEARD`, never `PICKED UP`. Registered as **B79**.

★★★★★ **THE SECOND FINDING IS A FALSE *NEGATIVE* ON THE ALARM PATH, AND IT IS THE ONE I WOULD SEND BACK: `match_channel_failed` HAD NO CORRELATOR AT ALL.** The plan's signature is `(FailReason, now_ms, out)` — state + window, nothing else — so **any DM's `send_failed` arriving inside the 8 s window terminated an awaiting alarm as `channel_failed`**, i.e. TERMINAL `Emergency::failed` (§B72's own landing state), **destroying the two unspent transmissions of an alarm that was merely `blocked` and would have retried.** A console DM giving up `no_route` while the alarm waits is enough. The discriminator is measured, not invented: **every channel-side producer passes `/*dst=*/0` explicitly** (`node_channel.cpp:736`, `node.cpp:1545/1551/1557/1573`) and **every DM one passes the peer** (`node_mac*.cpp`, `node_cascade.cpp`, `push_send_failed`'s definition at `node.cpp:1986`), and node id 0 is reserved for an unprovisioned node so it is never a real DM target. ⇒ the signature gains `dst` and requires `dst == 0`. Registered as **B80**.

★★ **TWO PREMISES CONFIRMED RATHER THAN DISPROVEN — pinned by tests so nobody "tightens" them later.** ① **`kOutcomeWindowMs` MUST NOT bound an exactly-correlated outcome.** A team post's `channel_sent` arrives after up to `channel_reoffer_team_max_retries`(3) × (`channel_reoffer_delay_ms` 10000 + `channel_reoffer_jitter_ms` 2000) ≈ **36 s** (`protocol_constants.h:449-464`), and an e2e ack's deadline is 60 s / 300 s — windowing those would discard the outcome the alarm is waiting for. `accepted` never expires; only `awaiting` does (P6). ② **`match_blocked` must accept an `accepted` slot, and the plan's test was right.** On a `-t -g` post the team copy mints a ctr and stamps `_last_channel_origin_ms` (`node_channel.cpp:752`), which then blocks the GLOBAL copy on `channel_min_interval_ms` (`:633`) — a genuine `send_blocked` while `ctr != 0`. Restricting it to `awaiting` would have dropped it.

★ **RESIDUALS, each with a named owner** (nothing here is a live safety hole; all are registered so they are not rediscovered): **B69** unchanged — `channel_remote_mint` must render as `SENT` and no `Emergency` state carries that distinction, so the obligation still rests on UI-6/UI-7's channel path, which now at last has an outcome to receive. **B83** — the `late_ack` slot is bounded only by a CALLER obligation: spec §3.4.1 scopes the upgrade to *"while the sub-view is still showing"*, that lifetime lives in `firmware_ui.cpp`, so UI-6/UI-7 **must** call `close()`; deliberately not a second timer here (the tracker cannot see the panel, and an invented window would disagree with the real one). `close()` and the leak it prevents are both pinned by tests. **B83 also carries** the `awaiting`-DM residue: `tick()` releases the slot and invents nothing, leaving the model in `DmState::submitting` — unreachable from the UI (spec §3.4 sends by `team_local_id`; only a HASH-addressed send parks with `ctr == 0`), guarded for type-safety, reported rather than papered over with a fabricated reason. **And the offer-order obligation:** `match_blocked`/`match_channel_failed` correlate by window rather than by ctr, so UI-6 **must** offer every push to the EMERGENCY tracker first — stated in the header, untestable in one slot.

★★★ **WHY B73 NEEDED *BOTH* A MAPPING AND A VERBATIM FIELD — the brief asked only for "thread it through to `refuse_reason()`", and that alone does not fix the defect it names.** `RefuseReason` has **5** enumerators; `SendFailReason` has **18**. A mapping alone sends **12 of 18** reasons to `other`, i.e. *"asynchronous DM failure reasons are discarded"* would still be true for two thirds of them, and spec §2.1 rule 6 (*"the full `SendFailReason` reaches the UI"*, `:147`) would still be unsatisfiable. But replacing `RefuseReason` was also wrong: `parser` has **no** core equivalent (the line never became a `Command`), and mirroring an enum `command.h` documents as **append-only** is the parallel-enum fork U1 forbids. ⇒ **two alphabets, one write site:** `_refuse` for the panel's compact code, `_fail` for the reason verbatim, both set by `note_failure()`. Mapped are exactly the three whose **remedy differs** — `unsealable` (encrypt / get the key), `no_location` (get a fix), `queue_full` (retry). Pinned by an 8-row table case that checks **both** outputs for every row.

It now lists **all nine** kinds with **no `default:`**. Negative control: adding a tenth ⇒ `src/firmware_ui_model.h:228: error: enumeration value 'channel_tenth_kind' not handled in switch [-Werror=switch]`. ⓘ The `switch` inside `note_failure` **keeps** its `default:` deliberately and that is not the same hole: `SendFailReason` grows on **core's** schedule, a new reason is legitimately generic *to this panel*, and `_fail` carries it losslessly regardless — the alternative would make an append to a `lib/core` enum break a `src/` build.

ⓘ **Two observations for Task 8's bench matrix, not defects.** ① **There is no model-side delay between attempts:** `channel_no_relay` re-queues *immediately*, and the real spacing comes from the core's `channel_min_interval_ms = 10000`, which refuses attempt 2 pre-TX with `send_blocked{next_ms}` → the blocked path then supplies the honest countdown and consumes no attempt. So spec §4's *"auto-retry ×3 with backoff"* is satisfied **indirectly, by the core's rate limiter**, and the observable sequence on metal is retry → BLOCKED ~10 s → accepted, twice. Worth asserting on the bench, because a change to `channel_min_interval_ms` would silently change the alarm's cadence. ② **A `long_arm` inside a compose modal leaves the modal open underneath** (§4.2 pre-empts, it does not close) — the emergency screen must win in UI-6, and the modal then self-closes on its own inactivity timer.

★★★ **THREE CODE FINDINGS IN THE PLAN'S OWN MODEL — registered, NOT fixed, because each fix is a behaviour choice the plan does not make (C1/C2).**
1. ★ **B64 — a roster that shrinks between ticks silently RETARGETS a DM.** `activate()` reads `s.team[_st.cursor % s.team_shown]`. The modulo is load-bearing (it prevents the out-of-range read) but its effect is that a cursor left on row 2 by an earlier tick's snapshot, meeting a 1-row roster, sends "Are you OK?" to **row 0 — a different teammate than the one highlighted.** Pinned by test *"a roster that shrinks between ticks cannot index out of range"* so the behaviour is visible rather than latent. A clamp to `shown-1` is equally arbitrary; the real cure is re-anchoring the cursor when the snapshot changes (Task 6) or refusing the activation.
2. ★ **B65 — `_last_input_ms = 0` at construction can blank the panel on its FIRST tick.** `on_tick` blanks when `elapsed(now, _last_input_ms) >= kBlankMs`, and `_last_input_ms` is only ever written by a gesture. If `mr_ui_init()` runs more than 15 s after boot — reachable on the NV format-on-corrupt and OTA-heavy paths — the very first tick blanks a panel that has **never drawn anything**, and only a button press recovers it. One-line fix (seed on first use), but it is a behaviour change and the plan's Task-2 tests do not constrain it either way (they all tick at 1000 first).
3. **B66 — `back` is identified POSITIONALLY across a TU boundary.** `compose_gesture` leaves the modal when `cursor + 1 == n`, with `n` from `kDmTextCount`/`kChannelTextCount` **here**, while the strings live in `firmware_ui.cpp` (Task 6/7). Spec §3.2.2 calls adding a canned text "a one-line change"; it is **two places**, and getting it wrong turns `back without sending` into a send. A comment marks the coupling; the durable cure is one table with the count derived from it.

The finding stands and belongs to Task 3/4: the seven `Kind`s (`channel_relayed · channel_no_relay · blocked · dm_acked · dm_no_key · dm_failed · dm_timeout`) have **no representation for "accepted, no LOCAL handle, and whether anything flew is not answerable synchronously"** — the third `ctr == 0` producer, which is a **success** (a registered mobile's `-g` GLOBAL post: the home mints the ctr, `node.cpp:1565-1573`). Task 4 would have to either call that success `blocked`/`dm_failed` (the emergency machine then burns alarms on a delivered message) or drop it (a permanent `SENDING...`). ⇒ **Task 3 needs an eighth kind** (e.g. `channel_unattributable`) whose emergency-side policy is explicit. ⚠ Unreachable on the `MR_UI_TEAM_CHANNEL_ID` team-plane path the alarm uses, so it is a correctness-of-type issue, not a live safety hole.

### ⛔ THE TWO FALSIFIED PREMISES (spec §0 ① and ②) — this is why nothing moved

**Ⓐ `boards/` IS TAKEN — by PlatformIO, and this time the ownership is real.** `boards_dir` is a first-class PlatformIO project option, *"A storage for custom board manifests"*, default `${PROJECT_DIR}/boards` (`platformio/project/options.py:297`), scanned in `platform/base.py:143-157`. It already holds **`seeed-xiao-afruitnrf52-nrf52840.json`** (named by `board =` at `platformio.ini:97`) and **`nrf52840_s140_v7.ld`** (`board_build.ldscript`, `:98`). Subdirectories survive (the scan is a non-recursive `*.json` filter), so `boards/heltec_v3/` would *build* — but it plants our source tree inside a tool-owned namespace, **which is the exact objection §0 ① raised in order to reject `variants/`.**

**…and the grounds for rejecting `variants/` do not hold.** §0 ① says *"the nRF52 core **searches that tree** for `variant.h`"*. It does not, in this project: `adafruit.py:262-264` uses `$PROJECT_DIR/<build.variants_dir>` **only when the board manifest sets `build.variants_dir`** — and `boards/seeed-xiao-afruitnrf52-nrf52840.json` **does not set it**, so `variants_dir` resolves to `FRAMEWORK_DIR/variants`, which contains **no `Seeed_XIAO_nRF52840` at all** (14 Adafruit variants, verified). Our `variants/Seeed_XIAO_nRF52840/` is reached **exclusively** by the two hand-wired lines the spec cites as evidence of core ownership: `platformio.ini:117` (`build_src_filter += <../variants/…/variant.cpp>`) and `:137` (`-I variants/Seeed_XIAO_nRF52840`). ⇒ `variants/` is **ours already**, and it is already "one directory per board" containing exactly one board.

★ **The constructive consequence — UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS, owner ruling needed:** adding `"variants_dir": "variants"` to the board manifest hands that directory to the toolchain, which then compiles `variant.cpp` as `FrameworkArduinoVariant` and puts it on CPPPATH by itself ⇒ **`platformio.ini:117`'s `../variants/…` term and `:137`'s `-I` both DROP** (they must drop together, or `g_ADigitalPinMap` is defined twice). That is "adding a board = adding a directory" delivered through the toolchain's own hook instead of a parallel convention. **Not built, not gated — do not adopt on my word.**

**Ⓑ ★★ THERE IS NO BOARD TIER TO ABSORB.** §0 ② tabulates *"board — 25 uses — absorbed by a per-board dir ✅ yes"*. The 14 + 11 reproduce exactly as token occurrences, but **23 of the 26 sites are chip-family OR-chains in which the board macro is a redundant alias**, e.g. `device_nv.h:353`:

```c

```

Moving those into `boards/<board>/` would move **chip-family** code into a **board** directory — precisely the U1 duplication §0 ② was written to prevent, achieved by the mechanism it prescribes. ⚠ **The table also double-counts:** those same 23 sites are counted once under "board" (via the alias) and again under "chip/arch" (via the three chip macros), so the "25 vs ~65" ratio is a measurement artefact. Real site counts: **33 chip · 3 board.** And `BOARD_XIAO_ESP32S3` (2 occurrences, `device_fault.h:20`, `firmware_commands.cpp:342`) is missing from the table altogether.

⇒ ⛔ **`src/device_nv.h` must NEVER land in `platform/nrf52/`**: it would orphan the ESP32 and host arms and break a native test. It is not chip code; it is a portable interface.

★★★★ **A REAL DEFECT S4a SHIPPED, FOUND BY ASKING WHAT STAGE 2 NEEDS THAT STAGE 1 DOES NOT CHECK — and it is the brief's own rule pointed forwards.** `emit_hash_query` gates `_crypto_ready` on `want_pubkey` (`node_hashlocate.cpp`), and **stage 1 passes `want_pubkey = false`**. ⇒ a node with NO crypto identity was told `queued` + `accepted`, flooded the by-id query, and could only discover at stage 2 — in an RX callback, ~25 s later, with the ack long returned — that the MUTUAL exchange is impossible. **An ack may not claim what it cannot know; it equally may not DEFER a failure it already can.** ⇒ the by-id arm now pre-flights `_crypto_ready` and returns the existing `err_no_identity` (remedy: `regen`) **before any airtime**. ⚠ **This CHANGES S4a's behaviour on an identity-less node** — `queued/accepted` → `err_no_identity` — deliberately, and it is the one behaviour delta S4b makes to an already-landed slice.
ⓘ The other four stage-2 outcomes were enumerated and are **not** knowable at stage 1: `degenerate` depends on the answer, `tx_dropped` is transient, `encode_failed` cannot occur (the buffer is sized for the larger frame), and `no_return_route` is evaluated identically at both stages (S4a already widened its guard to `by_id`), so a stage-1 pass implies a stage-2 pass.

★★★ **THE ESCALATION IS *NOT* THE AUTO-RESOLUTION `§no-auto-reqpubkey` FORBIDS, AND THE ARGUMENT IS IN-SOURCE AT THE EMIT SITE** (`id_pubkey_intent_consume`), not in a doc a future reader will not open. That ruling (owner-ratified 2026-07-29) forbids a **send** silently escalating into a WANT_PUBKEY locate, because it would substitute on-air TOFU for the QR ceremony on a message the user marked `-e`. Here the operator **typed `reqpubkey`** — the verb whose entire purpose is that on-air fetch — so stage 2 is the *completion of the command they issued*, it is bounded, and it is reported. The four `want_pubkey = false` locate sites the ruling names are untouched and keep their tags. ★ **A future slice that deletes this as "auto-resolution" would be reversing a distinction, not restoring a ruling.**

★★ **THE TIMEOUT REUSES THE AGING SWEEP AND DOES NOT PRETEND TO BE TIGHTER THAN IT IS.** `age_out_pending_id_pubkey` sits on `kAgingTimerId` directly beside `age_out_parked_sends` — the same sweep for the same question ("a hash-locate that never came back") — so **no timer id is consumed** (the wheel is at `kCap 91` with 0 free). Budget = `park_reflood_retry_ms` (25 s = ONE flood round-trip by that constant's own derivation), **not** `hash_locate_giveup_ms` (175 s), which prices park + six refloods this intent does not perform. ⇒ the honest bound is the **interval** `[25 s, 25 s + rt_aging_check_period_ms] = [25 s, 85 s]`, stated in `protocol_constants.h` and not rounded away. The report is an unconditional **`!!`-prefixed `_hal.log`** line beside its `MR_EMIT`, reusing S1d/QA-P2's fix verbatim: `MR_EMIT` is device-stripped and `fw_main`'s sink is otherwise trace-gated, so an unprefixed report would be **invisible on metal under `debug off`** — a "no silent loss" claim that was already false once in this arc.

★★ **THE RING'S BOUND IS AIRTIME, NOT RAM, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS 4 AND WHY IT REFUSES.** Every armed intent is one H flood already on the air with a second queued behind it, so four concurrent unresolved by-id questions is already an aggressive load on this plane; the ring is a de-facto rate limit rather than a memory budget. A full ring **refuses loud** (`CmdCode::err_resolve_pending_full`, appended — the exhaustive `ord()` walker enrolled it automatically, which is the S1c instrument working) and **never evicts**: evict-oldest would silently kill a request the operator was told had been accepted, which is the entire class this arc exists to remove. Re-issuing the same `(id, plane)` **refreshes** rather than consuming a second slot (`park_resolve_request`'s precedent). ⚠ **U1-checked and `err_ack_ring_full` deliberately not reused for the third time in this arc** — same shape, different ring, wrong remedy.

★★★ **P2 — MY OWN "NO SILENT LOSS" CLAIM WAS FALSE ON METAL, AND QA CAUGHT IT.** I wrote that `_hal.log` is *"the one operator-facing channel `lib/core` has on metal"*. It is not — `fw_main`'s sink was `if (g_mr_trace_on) mrcon.println(m)`, so under normal `debug off` the deferred-loss report was **completely silent on hardware**. `_hal.log` is a DEBUG channel and I described it as an operator channel. ⇒ operator-critical `lib/core` messages now carry a `!!` marker and the sink prints those **regardless of trace**; the report is genuinely unconditional. ⓘ A prefix rather than a new `Hal` method: `log()` is the only text channel `lib/core` has, and widening the interface would force every implementation (device, sim, three test HALs) to grow a method for one message. Other equally-critical existing `_hal.log` sites ("beacon pack failed", "team M-frame with no team_id") are deliberately NOT re-marked (C1) — the mechanism is there for them.
ⓘ **The `-Wmisleading-indentation` warning at `node_hashlocate.cpp` PREDATES this arc** — count is **1 at `ea4be0c`** (before "id to hash part 1") and **1 now**; it originates in `546bb46` and sits in the mobile-reg name loop, untouched here. It is already inside the accepted pre-arc board warning baseline, which is why every A/B in this arc reads "identical".

★★★★★ **TX1's OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A REGRESSION, and the enumeration the dispatch asked for is what caught it.** The instruction supposed `tx_with_retry` might be all-discard, in which case TX1 would be inert for its callers. **It is neither `void` nor all-discard:** it already returned `bool`, and **THREE callers read it** — `duty_defer_fire` and both `do_data_tx` arms — each deciding *"arm the post-TX state?"*. Their existing `false` means **"not sent, but a re-send timer IS armed"**. Folding a HAL rejection into that same `false` would have suppressed `start_ack_timeout()` on a dropped DATA and left the flight with **no recovery at all** — for a retry-eligible frame the MAC timeout IS the recovery. ⇒ the return is **three-way** (`handed` / `deferred_retry_armed` / `rejected`) and the readers branch on `!= deferred_retry_armed`, which is **bit-for-bit their old `true`** — pinned by two `static_assert`s beside them, so a future fourth enumerator on the wrong side is a build failure rather than a silent DATA regression.

★★★★ **AND THE HARDWARE LAYER WAS UNREACHABLE BY EVERY AUTOMATED GATE — which is why it survived three reviews.** This repo's test HAL returned a hard `ok`; the simulator's `FirmwareNode::simTx` pushes onto an **UNBOUNDED vector** and can only answer `too_long` at len > 255, which no packer can produce. ⇒ a **scriptable `TxResult` was a prerequisite, not a nicety**. Clean corpus: **0** `tx_hal_rejected`, **0** `tx_deferred_lost` — structurally, and now stated with the mechanism. **Capability probe** (force the HAL to reject every flood): **7123** rejections reached, and reverting the propagation under that same poison returns **all 36 streams byte-identical to clean**, so the poison is otherwise inert and every delta is the fix. The behavioural isolation is s22's `"OK reqpubkey queued"` → `"OK reqpubkey error"`.
★★ **THE DEFERRED RESIDUAL, and the mechanism was a choice worth recording.** A frame ACCEPTED into the defer ring can still meet a full HAL queue when its timer fires, and unlike DATA an H query has **no MAC timeout** to recover it — so without a report the operator waits forever on an answer that can never come. Now `tx_deferred_lost` **plus an operator-critical `!!`-marked `_hal.log`** — ⚠ see the P2 paragraph below: my first version of this claim was FALSE on metal (the sink was trace-gated) and the marker is what repaired it. ⚠ **A bounded re-defer was REFUSED**: it would air an H query at an unbounded later time, after the operator has been told and plausibly retried by hand — duplicate airtime for a stale question — and it needs retry state plus a second timer path for a case no gate can reach. **Reporting the death is the honest product; re-sending a stale query is not.** A per-command push was refused too: correlating it needs a handle the frame does not carry, and `send_failed{ctr:0}` is precisely the uncorrelated shape B39 exists to fix (owed to B39, C1).
⚠ **`err_tx_ring_full` → `err_tx_queue_full`, one day old and renamed anyway:** **two** bounded queues can reject this command, so a name — or an operator hint — fingering one of them is a wrong diagnosis half the time. Same reasoning that kept it out of `err_ack_ring_full`, applied to over-narrow naming. Free under M3.
**Non-vacuity (the new arms):** discarding the `TxResult` again reddens **2 cases / 9 assertions**; `lbt_complete` swallowing it **2 / 7**; removing the deferred-loss report **1 / 2**. Both HAL fixtures pair their rejection with a same-fixture `TxResult::ok` flight.

★★★★ **MY NONCE INSTRUCTION WAS CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY VOID, AND THE CODER FIXED IT PROPERLY RATHER THAN OBEYING IT.** I wrote: *"bind the sender's hash into the AAD so two members' nonces cannot collide."* **That cannot work.** XChaCha20's keystream is `f(key, nonce)`; **AAD enters only the Poly1305 tag.** ⇒ AAD binding **cannot prevent keystream reuse** — it would have detected nothing and prevented nothing, while reading like a mitigation. ★ **What was built instead: `channel_msg_id` occupies the nonce's 32-bit slot** (`nonce = BLAKE2b(seed8 | seal_ctr LE2 | channel_msg_id LE4)[:24]`), and the msg-id is `origin<<24 | (sender key_hash32 & 0xffff)<<8 | ctr8` ⇒ **24 sender-distinguishing bits, differing per sender AND per post**, and in the clear so every reader derives it. ★★ **Proven by COUNTERFACTUAL, which is what makes it evidence:** a native test shows two members with the same key, the same forced seed and the same ctr get **different** nonces via the msg-id — **and that the settled shape (team-key hash in that slot) produces IDENTICAL nonces, i.e. textbook keystream reuse.** ⇒ **the instruction to "stop rather than ship a weaker nonce" was honoured by shipping a STRONGER one and proving the difference.** ★ **Durable: a shared-key design makes the NONCE the only place sender-distinguishing entropy can live. AAD authenticates; it does not separate keystreams.**

★★★ **MY `want_crypt` FORMULA WOULD HAVE CAUSED A REGRESSION the moment a node acquired a key.** I specified `(c.crypt == on) || (crypt_cfg && key_held)`. Measured consequence: a plain **GLOBAL** post from a keyholder → `want_crypt` true, `want_team` false → refused **`no_team`** (a keyholder could no longer post to a global channel **at all**); and `-t -g` → refused **`global_clear_copy`** (a working invocation starts failing **because a key arrived**). Both are rows the spec itself marks *"unchanged"*. Built correctly as `(c.crypt == on) || (want_team && !want_global && _cfg.team_channel_crypt && key_held)`. ⇒ **and my follow-on claim that "the refusal strings' scope widens" is therefore also false** — correctly scoped, both permanent refusals still fire for **explicit `-e` only**, and CL1's wording stands unchanged.

(2) A one-sentence paraphrase of a ruling is where rulings go to die: O6's ruling text and its RATIONALE sat two lines apart in the spec, and compressing them inverted the meaning.** The spec now pins the ruling explicitly so it cannot be re-briefed wrongly.

**★★★★★★★★★★★ 2026-07-31 B29 (`§idbind-loop` — ★★★★ **A SHIPPED DEVICE HANG, FIXED IN ONE LINE**; **36/36 BYTE-IDENTICAL** — QA GO; uncommitted):** `Node::key_hash_for_id` looped `for (uint8_t i = 0; i < protocol::cap_id_bind; ++i)` with `cap_id_bind = 256`, so **`i < 256` was ALWAYS TRUE**, `++i` wrapped 255→0, and the trailing `return 0` was **unreachable**: on a miss it never returned. Fixed to `for (uint16_t i = 0; i < _active->_id_bind_n; ++i)` — the **verbatim idiom of its correct sibling `key_hash_of_id`** (U1). Native **1057/71046/0 → 1058/71061/0**. ★ **s18 keystone `1cd21235`/271629 unmoved in BOTH arms; 36/36 `cmp`-identical**; **`lus` md5 `15ec7b85…` IDENTICAL in both arms after 30 TUs recompiled** ⇒ **object-code proof the function is never emitted in the sim.** Boards 3/3 **ΔRAM 0**.

★★★★ **THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE RESULT IN THIS ARC: THE FIX COSTS FLASH (+16 / +32 / +16), AND THAT IS THE UB MADE VISIBLE.** My brief predicted *"≈0 or slightly negative — a bounded loop is not larger."* **Disproven, and the disproof is the point:** the loop was `const` and side-effect-free, so an infinite loop there is **undefined behaviour**, and **GCC was entitled to drop the termination test entirely** — the broken version compiled **smaller** because part of it had been optimised away. **The fix costs flash precisely because it restores a check the optimiser had licence to delete.**
★ **And the coder killed the noise hypothesis with an object-level control rather than arguing:** `firmware_remote.cpp.o` **11680 → 11688** (that TU carries **no** date stamp), `fw_main.cpp.o` 107136 → 107168, while `firmware_commands.cpp.o` — which **does** carry `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` — is **55028 → 55028**. ⇒ the delta is real codegen, not the ±32 B noise floor. ★★ **Generalisable: a UB loop can be CHEAPER than the correct one. "The fix should not add flash" is not a safe premise when the bug was undefined behaviour — and a ΔFlash that DISAGREES with intuition is evidence about the compiler, not noise to dismiss.**

★★ **A 3-ARM PROBE PROVED NEITHER HALF OF THE ONE-LINE FIX IS REDUNDANT** — exactly the discrimination the brief asked for, measured rather than asserted:
| arm | miss test | stale-tail test |
|---|---|---|
| `uint8_t i < cap_id_bind` (**as shipped**) | **HANGS** (killed at 45 s, exit 124) | FAILS — returns `0xBBBB2222` |
| `uint16_t i < cap_id_bind` | passes | **FAILS — same value** |
| **the fix:** `uint16_t i < _id_bind_n` | passes | passes |
⇒ **`uint16_t` alone pins TERMINATION; `_id_bind_n` alone pins the STALE-TAIL read.** Two defects, one line, two tests.

★★★★ **THE SLICE'S REAL YIELD IS A SHIPPED DEVICE HANG — see register B29.** `Node::key_hash_for_id` (`node.h:672`) loops `for (uint8_t i = 0; i < protocol::cap_id_bind; ++i)` where `cap_id_bind` is **256** ⇒ **`i < 256` is always true, `++i` wraps 255→0, and the trailing `return 0` is UNREACHABLE: on a miss it never returns.** Reproduced — a miss-case assertion spun the native suite **16 minutes** with no output. ⚠⚠ **And it is UB, not merely a hang:** the function is `const` and side-effect-free, so the compiler may hang, elide or return garbage, **differently per optimisation level and target** — untestable rather than broken. ★★ **The proof it was unintended is the NEXT LINE of its first caller** (`firmware_remote.cpp:196`): `if (!th) { … "unknown id (no beacon heard from it yet)" … }` — **dead code. A miss-handler for a function that cannot report a miss.** ⇒ **generalisable: a dead error-handler is EVIDENCE ABOUT ITS CALLEE. When a guard cannot fire, ask whether the callee can produce the condition — not whether the guard is redundant.**

★★ **MY BRIEFED "TRAP 1" NAMED THE WRONG TABLE, and being wrong found a second bug.** I warned that the hash→id reverse lookup could alias in **`_id_bind`**. ★ **The boot restore no longer LIES about provenance.** It used to hard-code `pinned` for every restored key; it now maps the stored value through `peer_conf_restorable`: `pinned`→pinned, `authoritative`→authoritative, and **anything else is SKIPPED and counted** — never widened to "not pinned means authoritative". ★ **Why that matters: `authoritative` is precisely what permits a DM to be SEALED**, so guessing it would manufacture a sealing capability out of flash corruption; and restoring a TOFU key as `pinned` would claim a human verified it by QR. A boot banner `peers = N restored (P pinned, A authoritative)` makes the one-time v2 loss **observable instead of silent**.

★ **`/mrpeers` is now HAMMERABLE, and the wear guard is per-record.** The second write trigger is the `peer_key_cached` push drain (precedent: `config_adopted` one arm below it), so an on-air key-learn now writes NV. `peer_rec_put` therefore returns an **outcome** and the caller writes only on `updated`/`inserted`/`evicted` — cheaper than `/mrcfg`'s whole-blob `memcmp` H3 guard (no second buffer, no extra read); the asymmetry is recorded beside that guard. ⚠ **And the store is deliberately RE-READ on every call rather than cached** — `factory_erase()` wipes `/mrpeers` behind this function's back, and a warm cache would write the wiped records straight back.

**Record-size caps CONFIRMED on both backends (they were an open question in the brief):** ESP32 NVS partition `0x5000` = 20 KB with a blob cap of **15,988 B** ⇒ 1160 B is comfortable, and `Preferences::getBytes` returns **0** (not a truncated length) on overflow, so `slot_size_ok` always catches a mismatch. nRF52 `InternalFS` is **28,672 B** total with **128 B** LFS blocks ⇒ `/mrpeers` grows by ~5 blocks (~640 B). **The nRF52 side is the tighter one and should be tracked, not rediscovered.**

★★★ **THE CLAMPING FINDING — exactly the trap the brief warned about, and the coder read the vendored source instead of assuming.** `crypto_x25519` (`monocypher.c:1546`) trims a **LOCAL COPY** via `crypto_eddsa_trim_scalar` (`:1469` — `out[0] &= 248; out[31] &= 127; out[31] |= 64`) and **never writes back**; `crypto_x25519_public_key` (`:1557`) *is* `crypto_x25519(pk, sk, {9})`, so it clamps too. ⇒ ★★ **monocypher clamps at USE, NEVER at STORE.** An unclamped stored scalar therefore **round-trips perfectly inside monocypher while being non-interoperable outside it** — which is precisely where T-K3 (the sealed key grant) and T-K4 (the QR) will take it. Fixed by **storing the CLAMPED scalar**, so the persisted and distributed bytes are canonical RFC 7748; clamping is idempotent (bit 6 of byte 31 survives `& 127`), so `adopt` reproduces the identical pair.
⇒ ★★ **THIS IS WHY THE BRIEF DEMANDED A KAT AND NOT A ROUND-TRIP: a round-trip test passes even when both halves are wrong together.** The shipped KAT is against **RFC 7748 §6.1**, feeds the RFC's deliberately **UNCLAMPED** Alice scalar, and **spells out the expected clamped bytes rather than borrowing monocypher's own constants** — so it cannot be satisfied by the implementation agreeing with itself. A second KAT runs both RFC parties through our function and reproduces the RFC's shared secret **K**.

★★ **MY NV PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS A REAL HAZARD I MISSED.** I briefed that `device_nv.h`'s `version >= 2 && version <= kVersion` range means *"a v21 blob still loads after the bump — verify the new fields default safely."* **Disproven: both backends ALSO require `n == sizeof(out)`**, and `sizeof(mrnv::Blob)` goes **208 → 272**, so a v21 record fails the **SIZE** check and is rejected wholesale — the version-range check never sees it. The real safe-default guarantees are elsewhere, and both were verified: (a) `mrnv::Blob nv{}` is **zero-initialised** at `fw_main.cpp:590`; (b) ★ **appending at the struct TAIL is LOAD-BEARING, not stylistic — the ESP32 `Preferences::getBytes` path DOES write the 208 stored bytes into the buffer before returning a mismatched length, so a MID-STRUCT insert would have splattered v21 bytes into the key fields.** A keyless node would have booted holding garbage that passes an all-zero check.

★ **THE ZERO-DRAW PROPERTY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT LUCK — and it was proven POSITIVELY, not inferred from byte-identity.** The sim's `team` verb **refuses `team new` outright** (`NodeRuntimeWrapper.cpp:778`: *"`team new` is deliberately unsupported: its random nonce would break scenario byte-reproducibility — name the id instead"*), so **no scenario CAN call it.** Execution-trace probe over all 36: `team_channel_key_derive` **0** · `team_channel_key_mint` **0** · `_adopt` **0** · `_load` **0**, with **two independent live controls**: same-TU `set_team_id` = **1** (s34) and ★ **same-seam `_hal.rand_bytes` (`node_hashlocate.cpp:399`) = 10** (s22 ×2, s27 ×8). **The same-seam control is the decisive one** — the corpus *does* draw `rand_bytes` ten times and team keygen contributes zero of them, which byte-identity alone could never distinguish from *"generation is broken and skipped."* The two claims are established separately: draws = 0 by probe, generation works by KAT + 19 native cases.
⚠ **RNG MODEL REFINED (mine was coarser than reality):** the sim's `rand_bytes` is a **separate per-node `mt19937`** (`_rng_bytes`, `NodeRuntimeWrapper.cpp:117`) from `rand_range`. ⇒ ★★ **THE RULE: AN ABSENCE ASSERTION NEEDS A PAIRED PRESENCE ASSERTION, or it is satisfiable by the thing simply not happening.** Masking 25/26 requires the forbidden event to stop occurring, and the only two routes to that are (a) the ack travels **team-internally** — correct — or (b) **no ack at all**, which asserts **11 and 19** fail on. So *(11+19: "the ack must reach TH")* ∧ *(25+26: "H1 must never see it")* can both pass **only** if the ack stayed inside the team plane. **That pairing is exactly what 13/14/20 lacked.** ⚠ Assert 28 is **honestly weaker and labelled so in-file**: matching on `dest` alone it cannot separate `_rt_team` from `_rt`, so it also forbids a legitimate static route to 101 — **over-strict by design**, because over-strict fails loud while under-strict passes silently. ★ It is deliberately **NOT keyed on `slot`**, and the coder quantified why: **~120 team installs corpus-wide read `primary`/`alt` against 9 reading `team`** (the `node_beacon.cpp:876/879` mislabel).

★ **s23_mobile_team_multihop being byte-identical is FORENSIC CONFIRMATION, not luck:** its only CTS length is **20**, a multiple of 4, so `ceil(20/4)=5` re-encodes to `(5<<2)|0 = 20` — the identical byte. QA verified.
★★ **WIRE PROOF — QA-reproduced independently.** In s19 the symmetric difference of every `tx.hex` in the corpus is **exclusively 20 four-byte cmd-`0x2` frames**; nothing else on the wire changed anywhere. Byte-3 arithmetic checks out and rounds UP: `19 → 0x14` (`ceil(19/4)=5`, `5<<2=20`) and `23 → 0x18` (`6<<2=24`). The coder reports the same exclusivity in **21 of 31** scenarios; the other 10 are event-count movers from contention re-ordering (s18 `rx` +566, `collision` +86, `tx` +76, **no emit type gained or lost**), and **0 assertion failures in all 31 before and after**.
★ **WHY the streams moved at all — and it is NOT "no change" as the spec implied.** Over every legal `payload_len` the reservation moves **−4 to −1 bytes**: a systematic 1–4 B *reduction* (the old `+13` over-reserved by more than quantization adds back), i.e. 20–82 ms less NAV hold. Still always **≥** the true frame length. That shortened hold is the whole stream delta.
★★★ **THREE PREMISES OF MINE DISPROVEN — two of them in the spec I wrote.** (a) **The spec's shortfall figures were 25–30% TOO LARGE**: they computed "needed" as `payload_len + 13` at the peer CR, **double-counting the very header fudge this slice retires**. Corrected: SF11/38 **−180 ms** (not −245) · SF11/120 **−549** (not −614) · SF12/120 **−1196** (not −1327). Direction and conclusion unchanged; the spec and `protocol.md` are corrected. (b) **"the full legal range 0..241" was wrong** — 241 caps the *inner buffer*, but `payload_len` is inner+**MAC**, so it legally reaches **249** under CRYPTED; the sweep runs 0..255. (c) ★ **I called `CTS_LEN6_MAX` "belt-and-braces". It is LOAD-BEARING:** `r.payload_len` is an unauthenticated wire byte, and unclamped `ceil(255/4) = 64` shifts out of the 6-bit field leaving `byte3 == cr2`, **which is 0 at cr5** — colliding with the "no hint" sentinel. (The sentinel itself holds for a different reason than I gave: `pack_cts` emits byte 3 only when `payload_len != 0`, so `len6 ≥ 1` ⇒ `byte3 ≥ 4`. Empirically zero byte-3==0 CTSes across all 31.)
★ **AND A PRE-EXISTING SAFETY BUG FOUND EN ROUTE:** the old M6 clamp (`payload_len → 241`) **under-reserved a real 255-B CRYPTED frame by up to 5 B** — in the one direction NAV must never fail. Replaced with a byte-count clamp at `lora_max_frame_bytes`, with the DoS ceiling proven *identical* (a forged hint now buys exactly what an absent hint already buys).
**Invariant sweep (the whole scheme rests on it):** cr 5..8 × `payload_len` 0..255 × APP × CRYPTED, ground truth from a **real `pack_data` frame** so a header-layout change fails the test — **40306 assertions**, `decoded ≥ true_bytes` and `≤ +4` for every physically-sendable frame. ★ It found a boundary I did not anticipate: at `payload_len` 253..255 the clamp makes the decoded length point *down* (to 252) — safe and documented, since such a frame is ≥261 B and unsendable, reachable only via a forged RTS byte which the byte-count `min()` already pins to a full-frame reservation.
**NAV table (cr5 overhearer, cr8 peer, BW250k, RSF8) — every hole reaches 0:** SF10/38 −103→**0** · SF11/38 −180→**0** · SF11/120 −549→**0** · SF12/38 −410→**0** · SF12/120 −1196→**0**.
★★ **COVERAGE — the CR-sizing is INVISIBLE to the corpus, exactly as predicted.** Probes: encode **31/31** · length decode **11/31** · byte count **11/31** · fresh-CTS producer **31/31** · **CR on the wire only 2/31** (s32, s33) · ★ **CR used to size NAV: 0/31**, so the sweep + the new `test_dual_layer` test are its **sole** detectors. The sharp finding: s32/s33 *do* carry cr8 on CTSes that third nodes receive, yet perturbing the reservation there has **no observable stream effect** — the 11 scenarios where it *is* observable are uniform-cr5, where the decoded CR equals `active_cr()` anyway. ⇒ **OWED: a scenario with mixed CR *plus* a third node whose own CR differs from the cleared sender's *plus* contending traffic in that window.** A second honest gap: **CTS producer B** (the re-CTS / `_pending_rx` path) is **0/31 AND untested natively** — correct by construction, detected by nothing.

★★★ **MY BRIEF WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A QUARTER FIX.** I named one carrier — a buffered row served on a re-offer or `CHANNEL_PULL`. The payload is **copied forward at every stage** and each stage emits independently, so `do_data_tx`'s re-stamp reaches it through **four**: (1) the `_channel_buffer` row; (2) ★ **`_flood[]` state** — `flood_rebroadcast_fire` re-floods from **`fs.body`**, its own cached copy, and **never reads the buffer** (QA verified at `node_channel.cpp:996`: `enqueue_flood_m(fs.channel_id, fs.flavor, fs.id, fs.body, …)`), so an armed backoff fires up to `flood_backoff_ms` *after* the switch; (3) a staged **`_tx_queue`** TxItem, stamped at TX time i.e. after the switch; (4) the **`_pending_tx`** flight, one frame from the air. All four are must-scrub. ⚠ **And the gate could never have caught the shortfall** — see coverage.
★ **`_channel_reoffer_pending` — a fifth structure, cleared by NOTHING today** (not `clear_routing_state`, not `clear_learned_state`). It cannot re-emit (`channel_reoffer_fire` bails at `find < 0`) but it holds 1 of **4** slots until its 10 s+jitter timer fires, so `team new` + a prompt post can hit `channel_reoffer_table_full` and lose coverage repair. Now scrubbed.
★★ **`team 0` (LEAVE) IS THE WORSE CASE, not the symmetric one.** With `team_id == 0`, `pack_m` writes `team_id` 0 onto a team-flavored frame and `same_team(0)` is false everywhere ⇒ it parses as a **plain leaf message ingested by every static node on the leaf** — a containment breach, not a leak into one team. `do_data_tx` now **REFUSES** it outright (C2), deliberately **not** `MR_FEAT_TEAM`-gated: a `!MR_FEAT_TEAM` gateway can buffer a malformed flavor-team/`team_id`-0 row off the air, and the guard makes it unservable rather than re-broadcast (costs the three `gateway_*` envs +92 B — worth it).
**Predicate, and QA's reasoning CONFIRMED at source:** `e.team_id != 0 || (e.flavor & channel_flavor_team)` — **no old-id comparison needed**. The ingest gate (`node_channel.cpp:192`) requires `_cfg.is_mobile && _cfg.team_id == m.team_id` and origination (`:302`) is gated on `_cfg.team_id != 0`; both stamp the team live at that instant, and `set_team_id()` is the **only** live writer of `_cfg.team_id` (`fw_main.cpp:603` writes it pre-`on_init`, when every table is empty). ⇒ every team row at a switch belongs to the team being left. Both signals are OR'd because `team_id` is the semantic scope while the **flavor bit** is what `do_data_tx` keys the re-stamp on — the OR means no row can be team-flavored on the wire yet survive here as "leaf". Genuine leaf rows have neither and **survive** (proven three ways in tests, plus the pre-existing `channel_buffer_count() == 1` assertion in the static-plane-survives test stays green).
**Audit — the structures deliberately NOT touched, each with its reason:** `_channel_pull_pending` is harmless **by construction** (its ids are *disjoint* from buffered rows — scheduled only on `find < 0`, cancelled on ingest — so there is literally nothing to scrub) · `_channel_pull_recent` is **kept on purpose**: it is pure suppression, and keeping it *prevents* re-pulling what we just dropped · `_per_origin_channel` stays per 27zb's ruling (bare-origin key, no plane bit, TTL'd, suppress-only) ⚠ with a noted knock-on: `do_send_channel`'s self-cap counts **buffer** rows, so the purge *relaxes* it — intended, and the untouched `_last_channel_origin_ms` keeps the 10 s floor as backstop · `seen_by[32]` is per-row and whole-row drops keep the id-spaces unmixed · the BCN digest's `dirty`/`bcn_ad_count` ride the row and an already-aired ad fails **closed** (`handle_channel_pull` serves only what it finds) · inbox `record_channel` rows are durable app history, never a re-emit source — leaving team A must not erase its messages.

★★★ **SEVENTH INSTANCE OF THE SWEEP-SCOPE META-BUG — MINE, and the sharpest yet: the faulty scope was an INDIRECTION.** I published what I called an audit of *"EVERY `active_cr()` use in `lib/core`"* — 26 hits, each classified. It missed `node_mac_rx.cpp:64`, the **RTS half of the very ledger I singled out**, because that site reaches `active_cr()` *inside* `airtime_routing_ms()` (`node_mac.cpp:44`) and is therefore invisible to a grep for `active_cr()`. Billing the ledger's DATA half at the sender's CR and its RTS half at ours would have been incoherent. The coder found it by sweeping all 21 `airtime_routing_ms` sites instead. **Prior flavours: directory scope (26n) · flag scope — `-Wswitch` is blind behind `default:` (26s) · path form — absolute vs relative (26t) · build profile — `#if MR_N_LAYERS>=2` (26x). ★★ **THE ONE SITE THAT CANNOT BE FIXED — and it fails in the DANGEROUS direction.** `nav_duration_cts`'s two `handle_cts` callers must size a third party's DATA at that party's CR, and **the CTS has zero free bits** (verified at `pack_cts`: nibble fully spent on `(sf−5)<<1 | already_received`; `tx_id`/`rx_id`/`payload_len` whole bytes; `parse_cts` accepts exactly 3 or 4 B). Against a heavier-CR peer the overhearer **UNDER-reserves and releases NAV while the DATA is still on the air** — i.e. the hidden-terminal collision NAV exists to prevent, failing in the one case it is for. Measured (cr5 overhearer, cr8 peer, BW250k): SF11/38 B reserves **690 ms for a 935 ms frame = −245 ms** (the same order as 27z's 246 ms DATA-wait hole); SF11/120 B −614 ms; **SF12/120 B −1327 ms**. Bounded only by LBT's physical backstop and the `payload_len==0` 255-B branch — but a NAV-enabled CTS *does* carry `payload_len`, so **the common case is exact and fully exposed**. Cost to close: a 5th conditional CTS byte (flag day, taxes every CTS in every mesh) or reclaiming the load-bearing `already_received`. **Documented at the helper and at both callers; OPEN for the owner.**
**Coverage — probes, honest:** FLOOD retune **5/30** move (validated by s33) · ledger DATA **24/30** (validated by s32+s33) · M_BCAST retune **5/30** move but **0/30 value-coverage** (executes 677× yet every sender is cr5) · ledger RTS **0/30** · NAV-from-RTS **0/30** ⇒ **native tests are the sole detector for three of the six.** Two probes moved **0/30 and the sites are genuinely DEAD**, not weakly probed: `reserve_yield_enable` and `flood_yield_grab_enable` are both compile-time `0` and the corpus emits zero `reserve_yield` events. **Owed: a scenario where a cr8 node answers a `CHANNEL_PULL`.** Closed accounting — decoding `cr_adv` from every RTS's wire hex: **8326 frames, 8312 cr5, 14 cr8** (10 FLOOD → the s33 win; 4 UNICAST+RELAY → exactly the 4 changed ledger records).

⚠ **Also deferred + documented in-source:** the **ACK-timeout** site (`node_mac.cpp:1287`) — its dominant term is our *own* DATA where `active_cr()` is correct; only the small `airtime_routing_ms(3)` ACK term is the peer's, and in the gateway-high-CR shape it **over**-waits (fail-safe). ★ **A coder self-correction worth keeping:** it first wrote in-source that the global `radio_cr` "has NO range check anywhere" — **false**. `cfg set cr` refuses outside 5..8 fail-loud and `gateway cr0=/cr1=` is validated via `GwValErr::bad_cr` **before** the NV write. The real gap is narrow and **pre-existing**: the NV load (`fw_main.cpp:597`, `cfg.radio_cr = nv.cr` verbatim), the sim's `map_cr`, and the public `Node::set_radio_cfg()`. Not worsened here, not fixed.
**Security note (bounded, pre-existing shape):** the advertised CR is attacker-controlled but can only make a receiver **over**-wait (≤1.6× on the payload term), inflating its `_pending_rx` hold and BUSY_RX `busy_for`. It cannot *shorten* a window. Same class the code already bounds — `start_pending_rx_expiry` already clamps `payload_len` for exactly this reason ("M6: so a forged 255 can't inflate the pending-RX expiry"). No new clamp added.

**★★★★ 2026-07-27y (owner finding #3 — CR REMOVED from the gateway window-split weighting — QA GO; uncommitted):** owner ruling 2026-07-27: *"window split needs to take parameters which modify airtime — SF and BW! However CR should be ignored (clearly marked in code) — different CR settings are compatible."* **The semantic diff is 3 lines** (`lib/core/node.cpp`: `eff_cr` deleted, both layers now weigh at the global `radio_cr`), wrapped in a comment block recording the rule, the rationale, the deliberate non-goal and the measured residual. ★ **ONLY `s32` MOVED: `54643800`/3100 → `68753f54`/3015**; the other 28 are `cmp`-identical at the 26w anchors, 0 assertion failures each (QA reproduced all 29). Derived windows (period 12000): **gw_4 3188/8812 → 4395/7605 ms**, gw_5 6201/5799 → 7604/4396.
★ **MY ALGEBRA WAS DISPROVED — and the real reason for inertness is stronger than mine.** I claimed the CR factor "cancels exactly" in `w0/(w0+w1)`. It does **not**: `airtime_ms` floors twice, so `per_byte_air` is only ~linear in cr (off by ±1 ms in **156 of 320** sf×bw×cr combinations), and varying the **shared global** cr 5→8 moves the split in **544 of 576** realistic configs, by up to **93 ms of a 15 s period** (poison probe P2 confirms: global cr 5→8 moves **8/29** scenarios). The slice is inert not by cancellation but by **INPUT IDENTITY** — where neither layer overrides `cr`, `eff_cr()` already returned `radio_cr`, so the arguments to `airtime_ms` are bit-identical before and after (verified over 4096 configs). The residual global-cr sensitivity is **pre-existing, unchanged, and symmetric**, so it can never favour one layer; what the rule removes is the **per-layer** differential, which was neither symmetric nor small.
★★★ **A REAL FIRMWARE BUG THAT CONTRADICTS THE RULING'S PREMISE — found by chasing s32's joiner failure, reported NOT fixed (needs a design call).** `start_pending_rx_expiry` (`lib/core/node_mac.cpp:1307`) sizes the **receiver's** DATA wait with **`active_cr()` — the RECEIVER's own CR**: `airtime_ms(sf, active_bw_hz(), active_cr(), …)`. In s32, gw_4 transmits on layer 5 at **cr8** while the layer-5 leaves receive at the global **cr5**, so a leaf arms **~746 ms** for a frame that needs **~975 ms** (SF11/BW250k) and abandons it → `data_rx_timeout`. **⇒ "different CR settings are compatible" is TRUE at the LoRa PHY (the explicit header carries CR and the radio auto-detects it) but FALSE in this firmware's RX-window sizing.** Same pattern at `node_mac.cpp:1287` (ACK timeout) and `node_mac_rx.cpp:148/176`. ⇒ **per-layer CR does not work end-to-end today, independently of the window split.** Options: advertise the peer's CR, or size RX windows for worst-case CR4/8. **The ruling's CONCLUSION still stands** (a layer's private CR must not take its peer's window); only its stated rationale needs this fix to become true.
★ **JOINER ASSERTIONS: DO NOT RESTORE — my hypothesis was wrong.** I expected removing CR from the weighting might revive s32's cross-layer joiner deliveries. **They fail both before AND after**: no `push[msg_recv]` carries either payload in either run (the only hits are `cmd_reply` echoes). What DID improve is real and worth recording: gw_4's `xl_bridge` **207245 → 133780 ms**, `gateway_layer_window_deferred` **10 → 0**, `tx_gateway_schedule_defer` **14 → 2**, `peer_suspect_mark` **36 → 22** — and the failure **moved and became visible**: gw_4 now reaches the last mile and gives up explicitly (`send_failed`, `path_cascade_exhausted`, `data_ack_giveup` all 0→1) instead of the run ending before it got there. s32's `_desc` is corrected accordingly (verified `_desc` is stream-neutral: the md5 is unchanged by the rewrite).
**Coverage:** probe P1 (`per_byte_air` +7) moves **8/29** — the derive is genuinely executed, but note **s27 does NOT move** (its gateways do not leave both windows at 0), so the derive is narrower than "every gateway". For the **per-layer CR rule specifically the ONLY regression detector is the new native test** — s32 is the sole scenario with a per-layer `cr` and it asserts no delivery. The new test is **non-vacuous**: compiled against pre-slice behaviour it fails **19 assertions**, matching the 4+3+1 override combinations.

Bridge soundness is pinned by **twin `static_assert`s** (one per namespace: `sizeof==1` + `join_adopted==13`), **proven to bite** (poisoning 13→12 fails both TUs). `ConsoleNames.h` states a HARD LIMIT in-source: **enum mappers only** — the lib is built with the NORMAL variant's `MR_N_LAYERS=1` layout, so nothing taking a `Node`/`NodeConfig`/`Push` may cross it. ★ **Side benefit: this closes the long-standing "the sim compiles no `lib/console`" blind region** — for that one function.

Corroborated by the coder three ways: `drop_bw_mismatch == 0` corpus-wide; an instrumented counter shows `bw_mismatch = 0` in **all 29** while the gate is evaluated **431,246×**; and #7-alone is `cmp`-identical on **29/29**. **⇒ 100% of the re-anchor above is #6.** The false claim has been deleted from the source note.

That site sits **above** `notifyRxStart` and the CAD `notifyChannelBusy`, so a BW gate there would exempt a BW-mismatched frame from the RX→TX turnaround charge and from marking the channel busy — granting 125/250 kHz layers the isolation only a separate **carrier** earns, and destroying the *"bandwidth grants NO orthogonality"* asymmetry I told it to preserve **in the same brief**. It went beside the **SF** gate instead, suppressing exactly the `PreambleDetected` callback; energy/LBT/collision/turnaround all still fed. Rationale in-source.

★ **A schema trap worth knowing:** `"layers"` is the array the config mapper reads (`NodeRuntimeWrapper.cpp:398` → `map_layers`, which maps `freq_mhz` at `:312`); **`"gateway_layers"` is `Disp::ignored`** (`:415`) — a dead key still present in s09/s31/s32. Per-node carrier uses the sim key `freq_khz` (integer); per-LAYER uses the firmware key `freq_mhz` (see 26u for why the two differ).
★★ **s31 — CARRIER ISOLATION PROVEN, and the physics is better than expected.** Layer 4 @ **868.0**, layer 5 @ **869.5**; the l4_* and l5_* leaves stay in **direct RF range in the topology matrix** yet cannot hear each other at all. Result vs s09: **`drop_freq_mismatch` 0 → 238** while **`drop_sf_mismatch` 255 → 15**. ⇒ frames formerly rejected by the *SF* gate are now rejected **earlier, at the carrier** — which is what real hardware does (a radio tuned to 868.0 never sees a 869.5 frame, so it cannot "reject it for wrong SF"). ★ **All FOUR of s09's cross-layer bridging assertions still pass**, so the gateway still bridges while the leaves are genuinely isolated. **DELIVERY WENT UP, NOT DOWN** — `rx` 385 → 396, `collision` 3 → 1, `tx_deferred` 9 → 5 — because channelization removes cross-layer contention. (The coder had predicted a possible delivery *drop*; measurement says the opposite. Recorded because it is the first hard evidence the feature models the real benefit of channelization.)
⚠ **A QA assertion of mine was WRONG and the code was right.** I asserted `drop_freq_mismatch count == 0` at `l4_j1` (recipe rationale: "a layer-4 leaf never sees a mismatch from its own-layer peers"). It fires **36×** — correctly: `nodeMatches` also matches the *receiver*, and l4_j1 IS in range of layer-5 transmitters on the other carrier, so it SHOULD register mismatches. Replaced with the correct **bidirectional** pair (`l4_j1` ≥ 1 **and** `l5_j1` ≥ 1), which is the sharper isolation proof anyway.
★★ **s32 — the CR RETUNE PROVEN, plus an OPEN DESIGN FINDING.** Gateway `tx` events now carry **cr=5 (21 tx, airtimes 19–75 ms)** and **cr=8 (76 tx, airtimes 26–63 ms)**; **before Wave-4 #4 every gateway tx read cr=5** because the sim never overrode `set_rx_cr`. ⇒ ★ **OPEN FINDING — the gateway window scheduler does NOT account for per-layer PHY airtime cost.** Measured: **any** per-layer CR increase (tried **6, 7 and 8**) makes both cross-layer *joiner* deliveries fail, while the gateway's own `xl_bridge` emits and same-layer delivery still pass. Cause is airtime budget, not the retune. The two joiner assertions are therefore **REMOVED from s32 (not carved as reds)**; s32's job is to pin the retune.
⚠⚠ **CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — MY DIAGNOSIS ABOVE WAS WRONG, and the `_desc` in `s32_dual_cr_gateway.json` repeats the same wrong claim (fixed with the 26x slice).** I wrote *"the window split is derived from SF weighting only and does NOT account for per-layer CR/BW airtime cost."* **False.** `lib/core/node.cpp:96-104` (v17) already weights each layer by its **own effective SF, BW _and_ CR**: `eff_bw()`/`eff_cr()` fall back to the global, and `per_byte_air()` = `airtime_ms(routing_sf, eff_bw, eff_cr, …, 240) − airtime_ms(…, 120)`. **The real mechanism is REDISTRIBUTION OF A FIXED PERIOD:** the derive splits `window_period_ms` between the two layers pro-rata, so a heavier CR on layer 1 **lengthens layer 1's window at the expense of layer 0's** — the cycle never grows. The cross-layer joiner exchange needs BOTH windows, so shrinking one breaks it. ⇒ the owner's 26x ruling (drop CR from the weighting) addresses exactly this, and is a *removal*, not the addition I described.

Plus the **CR runtime-retune** gap closed. ★★ **This REVERSES the documented decision at `hal.h:87`** (*"the SIM Hal does NOT model RF frequency… so it correctly inherits the no-op"*) — that text is now explicitly marked RETIRED in-source so the override is not read as a bug.
★★★ **A REAL FIRMWARE BUG FOUND — reported, deliberately NOT fixed (QA's STOP rule), and QA CONFIRMED IT AT SOURCE.** `Node::activate_layer` (`lib/core/node.cpp:488`) calls `set_rx_freq` **only `if (L.freq_mhz > 0.0)`**, while the two lines below call `set_rx_bw(active_bw_hz())` / `set_rx_cr(active_cr())` **unconditionally with the EFFECTIVE value** — and their own comment says why: *"NOT `if (L.bw_hz>0)`: an inherit-leaf entered AFTER an override-leaf must RESET the HAL back to the global."* **Frequency has exactly the bug its neighbours' comment warns against, and cannot be fixed the same way: `NodeConfig` has `radio_bw_hz`/`radio_cr` but NO `radio_freq_mhz`** (verified — the boot carrier lives in the HAL, not the Node). ⚠⚠ **CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — MY METAL-REACHABILITY CLAIM WAS WRONG, and I had reported it to the owner as a live metal bug. Retracted, verified at source.** I wrote *"ON METAL, a gateway with `layers[0].freq_mhz=868.1` and `layers[1].freq_mhz=0` runs layer 1's ENTIRE window on layer 0's carrier — reachable today."* **It is NOT reachable via the NV path**: `src/fw_main.cpp:632/642` **pre-resolves the inherit at NV-load** — `layers[0] = nv.freq_mhz` and `layers[1] = (nv.l1_freq_mhz > 0) ? nv.l1_freq_mhz : nv.freq_mhz` — and those two lines are the ONLY firmware writers of `layers[0/1].freq_mhz` (the third hit, `node.cpp:454`, is `adopt_mobile_phy`: single-layer/mobile). Because BOTH derive from `nv.freq_mhz`, the asymmetry I described cannot occur. ⇒ my scenario-authoring advice *"state `freq_mhz` on BOTH layers — `0` does NOT mean back to the node's carrier"* is ALSO now false for the sim, since `_sim_freq_khz` is wired: `0` **does** mean the node's carrier.

**★★★ 2026-07-25k (FADING MEASURED ON METAL — v1 parameters ready; NOT YET APPLIED, activation still deferred by owner ruling):** the measured input for the §6.1.3 fading activation. Tool: **`tools/dm_delivery_breakdown.py`'s new sibling `tools/fading_from_logs.py`** (QA-owned), which turns raw firmware console traces (`t=… ms «rx <TYPE> … sf= snr= rssi=`) into the two numbers `LinkFadingState.cpp` consumes. Source: 5 owner-supplied captures (`dumps/`, gitignored) from **older firmware** — protocol behaviour in them is explicitly OUT of scope per owner ruling and NOT interpreted.

★ **RESULT — v1: `snr_std_dev = 0.35` dB on all links, `snr_coherence_ms = 0`.** Basis: **19 directed links, 1515 usable samples**, mean SNR spanning **−5.8 … +8.3 dB**; σ **mean 0.355 / median 0.368**, range 0.19–0.52, **stdev only 0.083**. Per band: weak (−10…−4) median 0.487 (n=3) · mid (−4…+2) 0.336 (n=9) · strong (+2…+10) 0.325 (n=7) — a mild rise toward weak links but well inside the spread, so **a single global σ is what this data supports; a σ(SNR) curve is NOT yet warranted.** Coherence 0 because **zero τ fits survive a conservative test across all 19 links** (details below) ⇒ at the cadence real traffic samples, each packet sees an independent draw, which is precisely the model's i.i.d. branch. ⚠ **Semantics, stated honestly: this σ is total REPORTED-SNR JITTER, not pure channel fading** — on a static path much of it is the SX126x SNR estimator. That is the correct thing to model anyway: the protocol consumes *reported* SNR (route scores, presence tiers, SF selection), so it experiences the lump sum regardless of cause, and the sim already models quantization + the +12 ceiling separately.

★★ **OWNER RULING 2026-07-25 — receiver 105 (`M2`) EXCLUDED as a FAULTY UNIT.** The data flagged it before the ruling: node 11, transmitting the same frames, is seen with σ 0.32 / 0.33 / 0.40 by receivers 58 / 79 / 39 — but **σ 1.07 by 105, at a middling +1.17 dB**, so it is not an SNR effect. Across its 4 links 105 reads σ median 0.84 vs 0.37 for all 19 others (**2.3×**), and its capture ends in a `Guru Meditation Error` panic. The owner confirmed **M2 was STATIC**, which rules out motion and leaves a hardware/firmware fault ⇒ excluded from the v1 numbers above. **Consequence: we still have NO motion measurement** — the mobile-regime σ remains unmeasured and is owed from the next hardware session (which is also when §6.1.3(B) activation was scheduled).

**Method traps the tool encodes (each reported, never silent):** saturation — LoRa PktSnr is untrustworthy above ~+10 dB and the sim models a +12 ceiling, so samples ≥ `--clip-db` are excluded and counted (**42 of the corpus samples were all-clipped series, correctly refusing to yield a σ**) · quantization — 0.25 dB grid, σ below ~0.15 dB unresolvable · censoring — deep fades LOSE packets, biasing σ **low**; periodic series (a mobile DISCOVER retry at a dead-regular **122 s**, beacons at ~287 s) make missing slots countable · **silent log drops** (`src/console_sink.h` drops a whole line when the USB FIFO is full and claims success) are indistinguishable from frame loss, so gap counts are an UPPER bound · mixed SF never pooled (this corpus: 16 links at SF6, 3 at SF7) · per-node clocks ⇒ series built strictly within a file, never across.

⚠ **Four QA errors found and fixed while validating against real captures — worth knowing because three would have silently corrupted the link table:** (1) **`origin=` is NOT self-identifying** — H frames preserve the originator across forwards, so `N1-1.txt` shows `origin=58` 54× while actually being node **39**; using it mislabels every link in the file. (2) **`»tx BCN from=` IS self-identifying** (a node's own beacon carries its own src, and beacons are never forwarded) — excluding it made two files fall through to the filename, and the filenames are role labels (`M1-1`, `N1-1` both yield "1"), not node ids. (3) a mobile's `[whoami] id=17` legitimately differs from its on-air `from=25` (home-leased local id) — **on-air wins** for link attribution. (4) the `to=`-vs-self cross-check raised false alarms on every file because **the trace is PROMISCUOUS** (nodes log every decoded frame, not only ones addressed to them); only a total absence of `to=self` is now treated as suspicious. Also tightened: the τ fit was emitting confident nonsense (a spurious **279 s** from ρ=0.99@0.12 s fitted against noise-level ρ=0.14@538 s) and the lag buckets were labelled by their edge rather than the real mean lag; τ now requires ≥3 well-sampled decaying points with genuine short-lag correlation, and **|ρ|>1 — impossible for a true autocorrelation, an artefact of normalising a high-local-variance subset — is flagged rather than used.** Cadence-gap detection was extrapolating across capture discontinuities (reported "16062 missing slots" on a 32-minute series); it now requires a dominant modal spacing and counts only short runs.

**NOT APPLIED:** no default changed, no scenario touched, `snr_coherence_ms` still 0 and every link still `snr_std_dev` 0 — §6.1.3(B) activation remains deferred to post-bench by owner ruling, so the numbers above are the *input* awaiting that slice, not a live change.

Harmless while nothing modelled TX→RX; **lethal the moment it is** — the originator is deaf until `own_end + 8`, so a reply starting at `end_ms + 0` lands inside the deaf window and every CTS/ACK dies. Fix = one expression (`just_pushed.end_ms - now`), provably inert for any non-deferred frame (`f.start_ms == now ⇒ end_ms - now == airtime`).

Concurrent is tested FIRST so `drop_halfduplex` classification is bit-unchanged and only previously-**delivered** frames can become settling drops — that ordering is what made the forensics attributable. - **`mean_hops` in DENSE scenarios is cascade-inclusive, NOT the delivered-path length.** It counts *distinct nodes that data_rx'd the DM as a next-hop* — in a sparse chain (s19) that equals the path (3); in a dense mesh (**s18 ~10, s17 ~10.3**) it also counts every next-hop a cascading/contending DM touched, so it reads ~10 even for short deliveries. **Gate on relative STABILITY vs these numbers**, not the absolute value. A big jump = routing churn to investigate.
- Cross-layer is measured via `tx_enqueue_xl` + the `(origin,ctr)`-matched `delivered` (the firmware preserves origin/ctr) — the `dm_delivery_breakdown.py` "cross-layer DMs: X/Y" line is the authoritative per-scenario cross-layer number.
